meta.title: Chilean Elections
sources: Wikipedia: Chilean presidential and parliamentary election articles 1826-2025
Servicio Electoral de Chile figures as reported there

presEras.label: The early republic
presEras.blurb: Congress chose the first two presidents outright; after that a college of electors did it, chosen parish by parish on a franchise limited to propertied literate men. Portales gave the republic a constitution in 1833 that let a president serve two five-year terms and effectively name his successor, and four presidents in a row did exactly that.

presEras.label: The Conservative and Liberal republics
presEras.blurb: Thirty years of decennial presidencies, still decided by electors, in which the Liberals slowly prised the church out of the state and Chile fought and won the War of the Pacific. Two of the elections on this page had a single candidate and were settled before polling day.

presEras.label: The Parliamentary Republic
presEras.blurb: Balmaceda's quarrel with Congress ended in the civil war of 1891 and his suicide, and for the next thirty years Congress rather than the president ran the country: cabinets fell constantly and the presidency became an office of arbitration. The elections stayed indirect throughout.

presEras.label: The presidential republic
presEras.blurb: The 1925 constitution gave Chile its first direct presidential election and a strong executive to go with it. What followed was the most competitive stretch in Latin America: a Popular Front in 1938, a Christian Democratic reform government in 1964, and in 1970 Salvador Allende elected on 36.6% and confirmed by Congress, which chose between the top two whenever nobody won a majority.

presEras.label: The dictatorship
presEras.blurb: Allende was overthrown on 11 September 1973 and Chile held no competitive national election for sixteen years. The single entry here is the plebiscite of October 1988, held under the constitution the regime itself had written, offering one name and a yes or no answer. The No won with 56% and the regime accepted it.

presEras.label: The return to democracy
presEras.blurb: Two rounds since 1989, and the Concertación held the presidency for twenty years before the alternation began in earnest. Voting became voluntary in 2012 and turnout collapsed to the forties; compulsory voting with automatic registration returned for 2025 and turnout went back above 85%. In December 2025 José Antonio Kast took 58.2% in the runoff.

legEras.label: Congress in charge
legEras.blurb: During the Parliamentary Republic the Chamber of Deputies made and unmade ministries, and the elections that filled it were organised by the parties that already held the machinery. Turnout figures of the period cover a small registered electorate.

legEras.label: The presidential republic
legEras.blurb: Proportional representation from 1925, a Communist Party banned from 1948 to 1958, women voting in national elections from 1952, and a party system that settled into three blocs of roughly equal size. The last election of the period, in March 1973, gave Allende's coalition 43% and neither side a way out.

legEras.label: The binomial system and after
legEras.blurb: The dictatorship left behind two-member districts that handed the second seat to the runner-up list unless the leader doubled its vote, an arrangement that froze the party system for twenty-four years. It was replaced in 2017 by proportional representation in larger districts, and the chamber has fragmented at every election since.
